Marissa — thanks for the ping. I reviewed Brightline's markup. High level: we can accept a conservative publicity carveout if we get a narrow, time‑boxed license for co-marketing purposes and an explicit approval SLA (10 business days). Proposed compromise (draft language below):

"Notwithstanding Section 7, Customer (Brightline) grants Redwood the non-exclusive right to reference the Customer's name and logo in Redwood marketing materials and case studies, subject to Customer's prior written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld and shall be provided within ten (10) business days of submission. Customer approval shall not be required for short product descriptions (1-2 sentence) used in sales collateral. Use of Customer logo in third-party or paid marketing channels requires separate approval."

I also recommend adding: 
- A 90-day gating for testimonial publication (as requested) — Redwood may draft suggested quotes after 90 days but cannot publish without Customer approval.
- A requirement to show product usage evidence for testimonial approval (customer-provided screenshot or support ticket ID).

If Sales wants a firmer PR window (e.g., 30 days post-signature), we can consider an exception but that requires documented executive approval from Brightline GC.

I'll assemble a redline of the Order Form and send back to you by EOD.

-David
